content_html:
ASRock Rack’s 4U16X-GNR2 shows how radically the definition of a “compact” AI server has changed. The platform compresses an eight-GPU NVIDIA HGX B300 system, two Intel Xeon 6 “Granite Rapids” processors, liquid cooling, high-speed networking, local NVMe storage, and redundant power into a 4U chassis—a formidable density proposition for enterprises building AI training, inference, and HPC clusters. ServeTheHome’s hands-on review positions it squarely in the market for organizations that need an established eight-GPU scale-up node rather than a loosely connected collection of accelerators.
This is not a server intended to sit in a conventional small-business rack, nor is it a product that makes sense as an isolated “AI appliance.” The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 is infrastructure: a dense compute building block designed to become one node in a carefully planned, liquid-cooled AI factory. Its appeal lies not merely in the Blackwell Ultra silicon, but in a system design that treats compute, GPU fabric, networking, storage, management, airflow, and serviceability as interdependent parts of one machine.

Overview: A Familiar Eight-GPU Formula, Updated for Blackwell Ultra​

At the center of the system is NVIDIA’s HGX B300 platform. This is the latest expression of the familiar eight-accelerator HGX concept: GPUs are mounted on a common baseboard and linked internally through NVIDIA’s NVLink and NVSwitch fabric, allowing them to behave more like a coordinated compute domain than eight isolated PCIe cards. NVIDIA describes HGX B300 as an eight-GPU platform using fifth-generation NVLink and NVSwitch, with up to 1.8 TB/s GPU-to-GPU bandwidth and 14.4 TB/s total aggregate fabric bandwidth. NVIDIA’s HGX B300 reference architecture also specifies up to 288GB of HBM3e per GPU, or 2.30TB of GPU memory per node.
That enormous pooled memory footprint matters as much as raw accelerator performance. Modern large-language-model workloads frequently become constrained by model size, context windows, key-value caches, batching requirements, and communication overhead—not just arithmetic throughput. An eight-GPU B300 node gives software a substantial high-bandwidth memory pool while retaining the low-latency links necessary for tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and other multi-GPU execution methods.
NVIDIA’s own DGX B300 configuration illustrates the scale of the underlying platform: eight B300 GPUs, 2.3TB of total GPU memory, two fifth-generation NVLink interconnects, and up to 144 PFLOPS of FP4 inference performance. The DGX B300 documentation is not a specification sheet for ASRock Rack’s chassis, but it provides an important reference point for the capabilities and expectations surrounding the HGX B300 ecosystem.
ASRock Rack’s value is in bringing that common HGX foundation to a system that emphasizes configurable cooling, front-access connectivity, dense storage, and operational flexibility. It is the sort of hardware where a few apparently minor mechanical choices can materially affect rack deployment time, cable management, and service procedures.

Why 4U Density Is a Big Deal​

A 4U server may sound physically imposing in a world accustomed to 1U and 2U systems. In the AI infrastructure context, however, fitting eight flagship GPUs and their supporting CPUs, networking, switching, storage, cooling plumbing, fans, and power subsystems into 4U is remarkably dense.
The distinction becomes clearer when comparing liquid-cooled and air-cooled GPU designs. Air-cooled platforms need large heatsinks, massive airflow volumes, and substantial internal clearance. ASRock Rack also showed an air-cooled 8U16X-GNR2 B300 design for facilities that cannot deploy liquid cooling, underlining the physical advantage that direct liquid cooling can offer. ASRock Rack’s announcement of the 4U ZutaCore version explicitly contrasts the 4U liquid-cooled system with an 8U air-cooled HGX B300 alternative.
For data center operators, halving the rack units consumed by a compute node does not automatically halve the total operating challenge. The electrical and thermal load remains immense. But it can improve the amount of GPU capacity available per rack, simplify scale-out planning, and reduce the physical footprint assigned to a cluster—provided the facility can support the liquid distribution, power delivery, and network fabric that such density demands.
That qualification is critical. 4U density is not a free efficiency gain. It shifts complexity away from bulky heatsinks and into coolant loops, manifolds, facility water design, monitoring, leak-detection policy, and operational discipline. The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 appears built for organizations that already understand that tradeoff.

Direct Liquid Cooling and the ZutaCore Alternative​

ASRock Rack offers two liquid-cooled variants of the 4U16X-GNR2. The version highlighted in the review uses a more conventional direct liquid cooling (DLC) approach, with visible inlet and outlet connections for coolant. The front-facing plumbing uses color-coded fittings—blue for incoming coolant and red for warmed coolant leaving the server—which is a straightforward but useful serviceability detail. ServeTheHome’s external hardware overview documents the connections and overall chassis layout.
The alternative is the 4U16X-GNR2/ZC, which uses ZutaCore’s two-phase cooling technology. ASRock Rack says this approach uses a non-conductive, non-corrosive dielectric fluid to remove heat directly at the chip, positioning it as a “waterless” liquid-cooling option for operators reluctant to introduce water into their cooling loops. ASRock Rack’s product announcement frames the system as an effort to address thermal density while reducing the perceived risk associated with liquid near high-value compute hardware.
The distinction is more than a marketing footnote. Conventional direct-to-chip liquid cooling can be attractive where facilities already have mature coolant distribution units and standardized warm-water loops. It can offer a familiar service model and align with existing data center practices. Yet it still places significant responsibility on connector integrity, coolant chemistry, maintenance procedures, and facility controls.
Two-phase dielectric cooling targets a different set of concerns. The promise is compelling: use fluid engineered to be non-conductive, avoid a conventional water loop at the chip, and potentially simplify risk management in deployments where leak anxiety or facility constraints dominate the conversation. However, operators should assess the entire operational chain—not merely the fluid properties. Vendor support, consumables, technician training, warranty procedures, monitoring capabilities, and long-term service access should all be evaluated before treating either cooling approach as inherently simpler.

Cooling Is a Design Requirement, Not an Add-On​

With Blackwell Ultra GPUs, dual server CPUs, memory, networking, PCIe switching, and storage concentrated in a 4U envelope, cooling is inseparable from system design. ASRock Rack retains substantial hot-swappable fan capacity despite moving primary heat removal to liquid cooling. The reviewed chassis includes large fan carriers at the sides plus smaller fan modules in the lower center of the system. The review’s rear-chassis examination highlights those hot-swappable fans and the resulting airflow paths.
That is an important reminder for prospective buyers: liquid cooling does not mean a fanless server. Airflow remains necessary for memory, storage, power supplies, network components, and other board-level hardware. The cooling loop addresses the highest-wattage devices, but the rest of the server still requires resilient air management.

Compute: Intel Xeon 6 Provides the Host Platform​

The ASRock Rack system combines the eight NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs with two Intel Xeon 6 Granite Rapids processors. In an HGX server, the CPUs are not the primary AI accelerators, but their role should not be underestimated. They coordinate operating-system services, manage storage and networking I/O, feed data to the GPUs, host control-plane software, and provide the PCIe and memory resources that make the complete node practical.
Intel’s Xeon 6 P-core family is designed for high-performance server workloads, with support for features including AVX-512, Advanced Matrix Extensions, DDR5, CXL 2.0, and large PCIe 5.0 I/O configurations. Intel’s Xeon 6 product brief lists up to 128 P-cores per socket in the broader family, up to 12 memory channels, and up to 192 PCIe 5.0 lanes in two-socket systems. Exact CPU selection, memory capacity, and I/O allocation in an individual ASRock Rack configuration will naturally vary by bill of materials.
For Windows Server administrators and virtualization teams, that host-side flexibility is consequential. AI infrastructure increasingly mixes GPU compute with data preprocessing, storage services, telemetry agents, security controls, orchestration components, and virtualized workloads. The CPU platform determines how gracefully those adjacent functions can coexist without undermining accelerator utilization.
Still, buyers should resist the instinct to judge an HGX B300 server by CPU core counts alone. In this class of machine, the host processors must be sufficiently capable and sufficiently connected; the critical performance story is usually the interaction among GPU memory, NVLink fabric, network topology, storage throughput, software stack, and workload behavior.

A System Built Around Balanced I/O​

NVIDIA’s HGX B300 reference design emphasizes a balanced PCIe topology that distributes connectivity across CPU sockets and PCIe root ports. It also defines eight PCIe Gen5 x16 links plus a Gen4 x2 link per HGX B300 baseboard. NVIDIA’s B300 system requirements make clear that the GPU baseboard is only one element in a wider I/O architecture.
This is why the dual-Xeon design remains relevant even in GPU-dominant systems. A poorly designed host platform can create bottlenecks around storage ingestion, management networking, NIC placement, or device locality. A properly engineered dual-socket implementation gives the platform room to keep GPUs supplied and connected without reducing the entire system to a collection of compromised tradeoffs.

Networking: 6.4Tbps on the Front Panel​

Perhaps the most visually striking operational detail of the ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 is its set of eight front-mounted OSFP cages rated for 800Gbps connectivity. The review calculates more than 6.4Tbps of aggregate front-panel bandwidth without requiring a separate PCIe add-in network card. ServeTheHome’s report identifies those eight OSFP connections as a defining feature of the chassis layout.
That is not bandwidth for ordinary client traffic. These ports are central to the system’s role as a cluster node. NVIDIA’s HGX B300 design uses eight ConnectX-8 SuperNICs, providing a one-to-one relationship between GPUs and high-speed network adapters, with up to 800Gbps per adapter. NVIDIA’s AI Factory documentation says the configuration is intended to maintain direct, high-bandwidth GPU-to-NIC connectivity for east-west cluster traffic.
In practical terms, that fabric is what separates a serious multi-node AI environment from a collection of powerful but isolated servers. During distributed training, GPUs on separate nodes need to exchange gradients, parameters, and synchronization traffic efficiently. During large-scale inference, high-speed networking supports model sharding, request distribution, storage access, and service scaling. Latency, congestion management, cabling, switch design, and collective-communication tuning can all affect results.

Front-Facing High-Speed I/O Has Real Operational Value​

Putting the highest-speed network connections on the front can make cable routing more manageable in some cluster designs, especially where cold-aisle service access and structured front-of-rack cabling are preferred. It also creates a visual separation between AI-fabric connections and rear-oriented power infrastructure.
But front-access OSFP connectivity is not automatically ideal for every facility. Network architecture, overhead tray paths, rack orientation, transceiver choice, fiber bend limits, and switch placement determine whether it simplifies or complicates a deployment. The key strength is not that ASRock Rack declares one cabling direction universally better; it is that the server presents a deliberate, high-density networking layout that planners can incorporate into a broader fabric design.

Storage and Serviceability: Designed for the Physical Data Center​

At the front of the chassis, ASRock Rack provides 12 2.5-inch U.2 NVMe bays. According to the review, two drives connect directly to the CPU while ten connect through the PCIe switch complex. ServeTheHome’s storage overview also shows the cabled backplane arrangement.
That capacity will not replace a purpose-built parallel storage system for a major AI cluster. It is nevertheless valuable for local dataset staging, checkpoints, caching, boot images, container layers, logs, temporary training artifacts, and inference model placement. In many deployments, fast local NVMe is essential for avoiding unnecessary pressure on shared storage and network fabrics.
The front panel also includes four USB 3 Type-A ports, VGA output, and a power button. These are not glamorous specifications, but they matter during bring-up, troubleshooting, and field service. A machine built for remote operation still has to survive the moments when an engineer is standing in front of a rack with a crash cart, removable media, diagnostic tools, and limited time.

Flexible Management-Port Placement Is a Quiet Strength​

One of the most practical features is the treatment of management and low-speed Ethernet connectivity. The system exposes a management port and two Intel i350-based 1GbE ports at the front, but internal Ethernet cabling permits those connections to be repositioned at the rear. The review notes that customers can use a mixed arrangement—for example, management in front with 1GbE at the rear—by adding or removing the relevant internal cables. ServeTheHome’s chassis walkthrough describes the feature as a way to support multiple data center cabling conventions without requiring separate chassis SKUs.
This is exactly the kind of design decision that tends to be ignored in headline specifications and appreciated by infrastructure teams. Management networks often follow different physical paths, security boundaries, or operational ownership models than data fabrics. Giving customers a means to place those ports where they belong can reduce awkward cable runs and avoid unnecessary procurement fragmentation.

Power, Redundancy, and the Cost of Density​

The rear of the platform is populated with ten 3kW 80 Plus Titanium power modules for redundancy, according to the review; its text labels them “CPUs,” but the accompanying context and image description make clear these are power supplies. The original walkthrough should therefore be read as documenting redundant 3kW Titanium-rated PSUs rather than an unusual ten-processor configuration.
The very presence of ten high-capacity power supplies tells the real story. This platform is designed for enormous electrical demand, fault tolerance, and the ability to maintain service through individual PSU failures. It also signals that purchasing the server is only the beginning of the financial commitment.
A successful deployment needs:

  • Appropriate rack power distribution, potentially including high-voltage three-phase feeds.
  • Power-capacity planning that covers worst-case node behavior, not just average utilization.
  • Cooling capacity matched to both liquid-loop and residual-airflow requirements.
  • A switching fabric capable of handling 800Gbps-class connections and AI communication patterns.
  • Storage infrastructure sized for model data, checkpoints, datasets, and retention policies.
  • Monitoring and orchestration tooling that can observe GPUs, thermals, fabric health, power, firmware, and workload behavior.

The power supplies are redundant, but redundancy does not erase dependency. The server’s effectiveness is inseparable from the upstream power and cooling systems around it.

Risks and Deployment Considerations​

The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2’s strengths also define its risks. This is an exceptionally capable platform, but it is not forgiving of incomplete planning.

Facility Readiness Comes First​

The first risk is treating liquid cooling as an isolated hardware feature. A direct liquid-cooled server belongs in a facility that can supply, monitor, and service the cooling loop correctly. Flow rates, coolant temperatures, water quality, connector procedures, leak response, maintenance windows, and spare-part policies should be planned before a rack is populated.
The ZutaCore variant may appeal to organizations seeking a dielectric, waterless approach at the chip level, but it is still specialized cooling infrastructure. It changes the implementation rather than eliminating the need for operational expertise.

Network Investment Can Rival Server Investment​

Eight 800Gbps OSFP connections offer extraordinary potential, but they also create an equally extraordinary infrastructure requirement. The server needs compatible transceivers or cables, high-density switching, sufficient uplinks, congestion-management expertise, and an AI software stack configured to use the fabric efficiently.
A B300 node attached to an undersized or poorly tuned network will not deliver the distributed-workload behavior its architecture is designed to enable. The node’s speed increases the penalty for fabric mistakes.

The Software Stack Remains a Core Part of the Product​

NVIDIA’s HGX platform documentation emphasizes not only GPU hardware but NVLink, networking, optimized AI software, fabric management, and virtualization support. NVIDIA’s HGX platform documentation includes dedicated materials for Fabric Manager, NVSwitch bridge patches, and shared-NVSwitch GPU passthrough virtualization. That is a strong indication that operating an HGX platform is a systems-engineering task, not merely a driver-installation exercise.
Windows Server environments can participate in enterprise AI workflows, particularly around management, data preparation, Active Directory integration, file services, developer tooling, and virtualized infrastructure. However, organizations should validate the exact operating-system, driver, container, framework, and orchestration combinations required for their AI applications before selecting an HGX platform. The hardware is powerful enough that software incompatibility, unsupported configurations, or immature operational practices can become the limiting factors.

The Bottom Line​

The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 is an impressive example of what a modern NVIDIA HGX B300 server looks like when density is treated as an engineering objective rather than a marketing statistic. Its eight Blackwell Ultra GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch scale-up fabric, dual Intel Xeon 6 host processors, 12 U.2 NVMe bays, front-access 800Gbps OSFP networking, configurable management-port placement, hot-swappable fans, and redundant high-capacity power design form a coherent platform for serious AI infrastructure. The original ASRock Rack system review makes that integration visible at the chassis level.
Its most important achievement may be its refusal to treat GPUs as standalone components. The 4U16X-GNR2 recognizes that AI performance is ultimately shaped by the entire node: GPU memory capacity, high-speed interconnects, CPU and PCIe topology, NVMe placement, network bandwidth, thermal design, power redundancy, and the ease with which administrators can deploy and repair it.
For enterprises, cloud providers, research institutions, and AI service operators with the requisite power, cooling, fabric, and software maturity, this is exactly the kind of dense eight-GPU server that can anchor a high-performance AI cluster. For everyone else, it is a persuasive demonstration that the path to Blackwell Ultra performance runs through data center architecture—not just through buying more GPUs.

A direct liquid-cooled server belongs in a facility that can supply, monitor, and service the cooling loop correctly. Flow rates, coolant temperatures, water quality, connector procedures, leak response, maintenance windows, and spare-part policies should be planned before a rack is populated. The ZutaCore variant may appeal to organizations seeking a dielectric, waterless approach at the chip level, but it is still specialized cooling infrastructure. It changes the implementation rather than eliminating the need for operational expertise.Network Investment Can Rival Server Investment​Eight 800Gbps OSFP connections offer extraordinary potential, but they also create an equally extraordinary infrastructure requirement. The server needs compatible transceivers or cables, high-density switching, sufficient uplinks, congestion-management expertise, and an AI software stack configured to use the fabric efficiently. A B300 node attached to an undersized or poorly tuned network will not deliver the distributed-workload behavior its architecture is designed to enable. The node’s speed increases the penalty for fabric mistakes.The Software Stack Remains a Core Part of the Product​NVIDIA’s HGX platform documentation emphasizes not only GPU hardware but NVLink, networking, optimized AI software, fabric management, and virtualization support. NVIDIA’s HGX platform documentation includes dedicated materials for Fabric Manager, NVSwitch bridge patches, and shared-NVSwitch GPU passthrough virtualization. That is a strong indication that operating an HGX platform is a systems-engineering task, not merely a driver-installation exercise. Windows Server environments can participate in enterprise AI workflows, particularly around management, data preparation, Active Directory integration, file services, developer tooling, and virtualized infrastructure. However, organizations should validate the exact operating-system, driver, container, framework, and orchestration combinations required for their AI applications before selecting an HGX platform. The hardware is powerful enough that software incompatibility, unsupported configurations, or immature operational practices can become the limiting factors.The Bottom Line​The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 is an impressive example of what a modern NVIDIA HGX B300 server looks like when density is treated as an engineering objective rather than a marketing statistic. Its eight Blackwell Ultra GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch scale-up fabric, dual Intel Xeon 6 host processors, 12 U.2 NVMe bays, front-access 800Gbps OSFP networking, configurable management-port placement, hot-swappable fans, and redundant high-capacity power design form a coherent platform for serious AI infrastructure. The original ASRock Rack system review makes that integration visible at the chassis level. Its most important achievement may be its refusal to treat GPUs as standalone components. The 4U16X-GNR2 recognizes that AI performance is ultimately shaped by the entire node: GPU memory capacity, high-speed interconnects, CPU and PCIe topology, NVMe placement, network bandwidth, thermal design, power redundancy, and the ease with which administrators can deploy and repair it. For enterprises, cloud providers, research institutions, and AI service operators with the requisite power, cooling, fabric, and software maturity, this is exactly the kind of dense eight-GPU server that can anchor a high-performance AI cluster. For everyone else, it is a persuasive demonstration that the path to Blackwell Ultra performance runs through data center architecture—not just through buying more GPUs.References​ Primary source: ServeTheHome Published: 2026-07-27T16:02:25+00:00

blocks.html_en: Overview: A Familiar Eight-GPU Formula, Updated for Blackwell Ultra​

blocks.html_en:
At the center of the system is NVIDIA’s HGX B300 platform. This is the latest expression of the familiar eight-accelerator HGX concept: GPUs are mounted on a common baseboard and linked internally through NVIDIA’s NVLink and NVSwitch fabric, allowing them to behave more like a coordinated compute domain than eight isolated PCIe cards. NVIDIA describes HGX B300 as an eight-GPU platform using fifth-generation NVLink and NVSwitch, with up to 1.8 TB/s GPU-to-GPU bandwidth and 14.4 TB/s total aggregate fabric bandwidth. NVIDIA’s HGX B300 reference architecture also specifies up to 288GB of HBM3e per GPU, or 2.30TB of GPU memory per node.
That enormous pooled memory footprint matters as much as raw accelerator performance. Modern large-language-model workloads frequently become constrained by model size, context windows, key-value caches, batching requirements, and communication overhead—not just arithmetic throughput. An eight-GPU B300 node gives software a substantial high-bandwidth memory pool while retaining the low-latency links necessary for tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism, and other multi-GPU execution methods.
NVIDIA’s own DGX B300 configuration illustrates the scale of the underlying platform: eight B300 GPUs, 2.3TB of total GPU memory, two fifth-generation NVLink interconnects, and up to 144 PFLOPS of FP4 inference performance. The DGX B300 documentation is not a specification sheet for ASRock Rack’s chassis, but it provides an important reference point for the capabilities and expectations surrounding the HGX B300 ecosystem.
ASRock Rack’s value is in bringing that common HGX foundation to a system that emphasizes configurable cooling, front-access connectivity, dense storage, and operational flexibility. It is the sort of hardware where a few apparently minor mechanical choices can materially affect rack deployment time, cable management, and service procedures.

blocks.html_en: Why 4U Density Is a Big Deal​

sentences.en: Why 4U Density Is a Big Deal​
sentences.zh: 为什么 4U 密度很重要​

blocks.html_en:
A 4U server may sound physically imposing in a world accustomed to 1U and 2U systems. In the AI infrastructure context, however, fitting eight flagship GPUs and their supporting CPUs, networking, switching, storage, cooling plumbing, fans, and power subsystems into 4U is remarkably dense.
The distinction becomes clearer when comparing liquid-cooled and air-cooled GPU designs. Air-cooled platforms need large heatsinks, massive airflow volumes, and substantial internal clearance. ASRock Rack also showed an air-cooled 8U16X-GNR2 B300 design for facilities that cannot deploy liquid cooling, underlining the physical advantage that direct liquid cooling can offer. ASRock Rack’s announcement of the 4U ZutaCore version explicitly contrasts the 4U liquid-cooled system with an 8U air-cooled HGX B300 alternative.
For data center operators, halving the rack units consumed by a compute node does not automatically halve the total operating challenge. The electrical and thermal load remains immense. But it can improve the amount of GPU capacity available per rack, simplify scale-out planning, and reduce the physical footprint assigned to a cluster—provided the facility can support the liquid distribution, power delivery, and network fabric that such density demands.
That qualification is critical. 4U density is not a free efficiency gain. It shifts complexity away from bulky heatsinks and into coolant loops, manifolds, facility water design, monitoring, leak-detection policy, and operational discipline. The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 appears built for organizations that already understand that tradeoff.

blocks.html_en: Direct Liquid Cooling and the ZutaCore Alternative​

sentences.en: Direct Liquid Cooling and the ZutaCore Alternative​
sentences.zh: 直接液体冷却和 ZutaCore 替代方案​

blocks.html_en:
ASRock Rack offers two liquid-cooled variants of the 4U16X-GNR2. The version highlighted in the review uses a more conventional direct liquid cooling (DLC) approach, with visible inlet and outlet connections for coolant. The front-facing plumbing uses color-coded fittings—blue for incoming coolant and red for warmed coolant leaving the server—which is a straightforward but useful serviceability detail. ServeTheHome’s external hardware overview documents the connections and overall chassis layout.
The alternative is the 4U16X-GNR2/ZC, which uses ZutaCore’s two-phase cooling technology. ASRock Rack says this approach uses a non-conductive, non-corrosive dielectric fluid to remove heat directly at the chip, positioning it as a “waterless” liquid-cooling option for operators reluctant to introduce water into their cooling loops. ASRock Rack’s product announcement frames the system as an effort to address thermal density while reducing the perceived risk associated with liquid near high-value compute hardware.
The distinction is more than a marketing footnote. Conventional direct-to-chip liquid cooling can be attractive where facilities already have mature coolant distribution units and standardized warm-water loops. It can offer a familiar service model and align with existing data center practices. Yet it still places significant responsibility on connector integrity, coolant chemistry, maintenance procedures, and facility controls.
Two-phase dielectric cooling targets a different set of concerns. The promise is compelling: use fluid engineered to be non-conductive, avoid a conventional water loop at the chip, and potentially simplify risk management in deployments where leak anxiety or facility constraints dominate the conversation. However, operators should assess the entire operational chain—not merely the fluid properties. Vendor support, consumables, technician training, warranty procedures, monitoring capabilities, and long-term service access should all be evaluated before treating either cooling approach as inherently simpler.

blocks.html_en:
With Blackwell Ultra GPUs, dual server CPUs, memory, networking, PCIe switching, and storage concentrated in a 4U envelope, cooling is inseparable from system design. ASRock Rack retains substantial hot-swappable fan capacity despite moving primary heat removal to liquid cooling. The reviewed chassis includes large fan carriers at the sides plus smaller fan modules in the lower center of the system. The review’s rear-chassis examination highlights those hot-swappable fans and the resulting airflow paths.
That is an important reminder for prospective buyers: liquid cooling does not mean a fanless server. Airflow remains necessary for memory, storage, power supplies, network components, and other board-level hardware. The cooling loop addresses the highest-wattage devices, but the rest of the server still requires resilient air management.

blocks.html_en:
The ASRock Rack system combines the eight NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs with two Intel Xeon 6 Granite Rapids processors. In an HGX server, the CPUs are not the primary AI accelerators, but their role should not be underestimated. They coordinate operating-system services, manage storage and networking I/O, feed data to the GPUs, host control-plane software, and provide the PCIe and memory resources that make the complete node practical.
Intel’s Xeon 6 P-core family is designed for high-performance server workloads, with support for features including AVX-512, Advanced Matrix Extensions, DDR5, CXL 2.0, and large PCIe 5.0 I/O configurations. Intel’s Xeon 6 product brief lists up to 128 P-cores per socket in the broader family, up to 12 memory channels, and up to 192 PCIe 5.0 lanes in two-socket systems. Exact CPU selection, memory capacity, and I/O allocation in an individual ASRock Rack configuration will naturally vary by bill of materials.
For Windows Server administrators and virtualization teams, that host-side flexibility is consequential. AI infrastructure increasingly mixes GPU compute with data preprocessing, storage services, telemetry agents, security controls, orchestration components, and virtualized workloads. The CPU platform determines how gracefully those adjacent functions can coexist without undermining accelerator utilization.
Still, buyers should resist the instinct to judge an HGX B300 server by CPU core counts alone. In this class of machine, the host processors must be sufficiently capable and sufficiently connected; the critical performance story is usually the interaction among GPU memory, NVLink fabric, network topology, storage throughput, software stack, and workload behavior.

blocks.html_en: A System Built Around Balanced I/O​

sentences.en: A System Built Around Balanced I/O​
sentences.zh: 围绕平衡 I/O 构建的系统​

blocks.html_en:
NVIDIA’s HGX B300 reference design emphasizes a balanced PCIe topology that distributes connectivity across CPU sockets and PCIe root ports. It also defines eight PCIe Gen5 x16 links plus a Gen4 x2 link per HGX B300 baseboard. NVIDIA’s B300 system requirements make clear that the GPU baseboard is only one element in a wider I/O architecture.
This is why the dual-Xeon design remains relevant even in GPU-dominant systems. A poorly designed host platform can create bottlenecks around storage ingestion, management networking, NIC placement, or device locality. A properly engineered dual-socket implementation gives the platform room to keep GPUs supplied and connected without reducing the entire system to a collection of compromised tradeoffs.

blocks.html_en: Networking: 6.4Tbps on the Front Panel​

sentences.en: Networking: 6.4Tbps on the Front Panel​
sentences.zh: 网络：前面板上的 6.4Tbps

blocks.html_en:
Perhaps the most visually striking operational detail of the ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 is its set of eight front-mounted OSFP cages rated for 800Gbps connectivity. The review calculates more than 6.4Tbps of aggregate front-panel bandwidth without requiring a separate PCIe add-in network card. ServeTheHome’s report identifies those eight OSFP connections as a defining feature of the chassis layout.
That is not bandwidth for ordinary client traffic. These ports are central to the system’s role as a cluster node. NVIDIA’s HGX B300 design uses eight ConnectX-8 SuperNICs, providing a one-to-one relationship between GPUs and high-speed network adapters, with up to 800Gbps per adapter. NVIDIA’s AI Factory documentation says the configuration is intended to maintain direct, high-bandwidth GPU-to-NIC connectivity for east-west cluster traffic.
In practical terms, that fabric is what separates a serious multi-node AI environment from a collection of powerful but isolated servers. During distributed training, GPUs on separate nodes need to exchange gradients, parameters, and synchronization traffic efficiently. During large-scale inference, high-speed networking supports model sharding, request distribution, storage access, and service scaling. Latency, congestion management, cabling, switch design, and collective-communication tuning can all affect results.

blocks.html_en:
Putting the highest-speed network connections on the front can make cable routing more manageable in some cluster designs, especially where cold-aisle service access and structured front-of-rack cabling are preferred. It also creates a visual separation between AI-fabric connections and rear-oriented power infrastructure.
But front-access OSFP connectivity is not automatically ideal for every facility. Network architecture, overhead tray paths, rack orientation, transceiver choice, fiber bend limits, and switch placement determine whether it simplifies or complicates a deployment. The key strength is not that ASRock Rack declares one cabling direction universally better; it is that the server presents a deliberate, high-density networking layout that planners can incorporate into a broader fabric design.

blocks.html_en: Flexible Management-Port Placement Is a Quiet Strength​

sentences.en: Flexible Management-Port Placement Is a Quiet Strength​

blocks.html_en:
One of the most practical features is the treatment of management and low-speed Ethernet connectivity. The system exposes a management port and two Intel i350-based 1GbE ports at the front, but internal Ethernet cabling permits those connections to be repositioned at the rear. The review notes that customers can use a mixed arrangement—for example, management in front with 1GbE at the rear—by adding or removing the relevant internal cables. ServeTheHome’s chassis walkthrough describes the feature as a way to support multiple data center cabling conventions without requiring separate chassis SKUs.
This is exactly the kind of design decision that tends to be ignored in headline specifications and appreciated by infrastructure teams. Management networks often follow different physical paths, security boundaries, or operational ownership models than data fabrics. Giving customers a means to place those ports where they belong can reduce awkward cable runs and avoid unnecessary procurement fragmentation.

blocks.html_en:
The ASRock Rack 4U16X-GNR2 is an impressive example of what a modern NVIDIA HGX B300 server looks like when density is treated as an engineering objective rather than a marketing statistic. Its eight Blackwell Ultra GPUs, NVLink/NVSwitch scale-up fabric, dual Intel Xeon 6 host processors, 12 U.2 NVMe bays, front-access 800Gbps OSFP networking, configurable management-port placement, hot-swappable fans, and redundant high-capacity power design form a coherent platform for serious AI infrastructure. The original ASRock Rack system review makes that integration visible at the chassis level.
Its most important achievement may be its refusal to treat GPUs as standalone components. The 4U16X-GNR2 recognizes that AI performance is ultimately shaped by the entire node: GPU memory capacity, high-speed interconnects, CPU and PCIe topology, NVMe placement, network bandwidth, thermal design, power redundancy, and the ease with which administrators can deploy and repair it.
For enterprises, cloud providers, research institutions, and AI service operators with the requisite power, cooling, fabric, and software maturity, this is exactly the kind of dense eight-GPU server that can anchor a high-performance AI cluster. For everyone else, it is a persuasive demonstration that the path to Blackwell Ultra performance runs through data center architecture—not just through buying more GPUs.

content_html_zh:
华擎 Rack 的 4U16X-GNR2 展示了“紧凑型”AI 服务器的定义发生了多么彻底的改变。 该平台将八个 GPU NVIDIA HGX B300 系统、两个 Intel Xeon 6“Granite Rapids”处理器、液体冷却、高速网络、本地 NVMe 存储和冗余电源压缩到 4U 机箱中，这对于构建 AI 训练、推理和 HPC 集群的企业来说是一个强大的密度主张。 ServeTheHome 的实际审查将其定位于需要已建立的 8 个 GPU 扩展节点而不是松散连接的加速器集合的组织的市场。 这不是一个旨在安装在传统小型企业机架中的服务器，也不是一个作为孤立的“人工智能设备”有意义的产品。 华擎机架 4U16X-GNR2 是基础设施：一个密集的计算构建块，旨在成为精心规划的液冷人工智能工厂中的一个节点。 其吸引力不仅在于 Blackwell Ultra 芯片，还在于将计算、GPU 结构、网络、存储、管理、气流和可维护性视为一台机器的相互依赖部分的系统设计。

概述：熟悉的八 GPU 公式，针对 Blackwell Ultra 进行了更新​

该系统的核心是 NVIDIA 的 HGX B300 平台。 这是熟悉的八加速器 HGX 概念的最新表达：GPU 安装在通用基板上，并通过 NVIDIA 的 NVLink 和 NVSwitch 结构进行内部链接，使它们的行为更像是一个协调的计算域，而不是八个独立的 PCIe 卡。 NVIDIA 将 HGX B300 描述为使用第五代 NVLink 和 NVSwitch 的八 GPU 平台，具有高达 1.8 TB/s GPU 到 GPU 带宽和 14.4 TB/s 总聚合结构带宽。 NVIDIA 的 HGX B300 参考架构还指定每个 GPU 高达 288GB HBM3e，或每个节点 2.30TB GPU 内存。 巨大的池内存占用与原始加速器性能一样重要。 现代大型语言模型工作负载经常受到模型大小、上下文窗口、键值缓存、批处理要求和通信开销的限制，而不仅仅是算术吞吐量。 八个 GPU B300 节点为软件提供了大量的高带宽内存池，同时保留张量并行、管道并行和其他多 GPU 执行方法所需的低延迟链接。 NVIDIA 自己的 DGX B300 配置说明了底层平台的规模：8 个 B300 GPU、2.3TB 总 GPU 内存、两个第五代 NVLink 互连以及高达 144 PFLOPS 的 FP4 推理性能。 DGX B300 文档不是华擎 Rack 机箱的规格表，但它为围绕 HGX B300 生态系统的功能和期望提供了重要的参考点。 华擎机架的价值在于将通用的 HGX 基础引入强调可配置冷却、前端接入连接、密集存储和操作灵活性的系统中。 在这种硬件中，一些看似微小的机械选择可能会对机架部署时间、电缆管理和服务程序产生重大影响。

为什么 4U 密度很重要​

在习惯了 1U 和 2U 系统的世界中，4U 服务器在物理上可能听起来很宏伟。 然而，在人工智能基础设施环境中，将八个旗舰 GPU 及其支持 CPU、网络、交换、存储、冷却管道、风扇和电源子系统安装到 4U 中是非常密集的。 比较液冷和风冷 GPU 设计时，区别变得更加明显。 风冷平台需要大型散热器、大量气流和足够的内部间隙。 华擎 Rack 还展示了针对无法部署液体冷却的设施的风冷 8U16X-GNR2 B300 设计，强调了直接液体冷却可以提供的物理优势。 华擎 Rack 发布的 4U ZutaCore 版本明确将 4U 液冷系统与 8U 风冷 HGX B300 替代方案进行对比。 对于数据中心运营商来说，将计算节点消耗的机架单元减半并不会自动将总运营挑战减少一半。 电力和热负荷仍然巨大。 但它可以提高每个机架可用的 GPU 容量，简化横向扩展规划，并减少分配给集群的物理占用空间，前提是该设施可以支持这种密度所需的液体分配、电力传输和网络结构。 这个资格至关重要。 4U 密度并不是免费的效率增益。 它将复杂性从笨重的散热器转移到冷却剂回路、歧管、设施水设计、监控、泄漏检测政策和操作规程中。 华擎机架 4U16X-GNR2 似乎是为已经了解这种权衡的组织而构建的。

直接液体冷却和 ZutaCore 替代方案​

ASRock Rack 提供 4U16X-GNR2 的两种液冷型号。 评论中强调的版本采用了更传统的直接液体冷却（DLC）方法，具有可见的冷却剂入口和出口连接。 前置管道使用颜色编码的配件 - 蓝色表示进入的冷却剂，红色表示离开服务器的加热冷却剂 - 这是一个简单但有用的可维护性细节。 ServeTheHome 的外部硬件概述记录了连接和整体机箱布局。 另一种选择是 4U16X-GNR2/ZC，它采用 ZutaCore 的两相冷却技术。 华擎 Rack 表示，这种方法使用不导电、无腐蚀性的介电流体直接在芯片上散热，对于不愿将水引入冷却回路的运营商来说，将其定位为“无水”液体冷却选项。 华擎 Rack 的产品公告将该系统定位为解决热密度问题，同时降低与高价值计算硬件附近的液体相关的感知风险。 这种区别不仅仅是营销脚注。 当设施已经拥有成熟的冷却剂分配装置和标准化的温水回路时，传统的直接芯片液体冷却可能很有吸引力。 它可以提供熟悉的服务模型并与现有数据中心实践保持一致。 然而，它仍然对连接器完整性、冷却剂化学、维护程序和设施控制负有重大责任。 两相电介质冷却针对的是一系列不同的问题。 这一承诺令人信服：使用设计为不导电的流体，避免芯片上的传统水回路，并可能简化在泄漏焦虑或设施限制占主导地位的部署中的风险管理。 然而，运营商应该评估整个运营链，而不仅仅是流体特性。 在将任何一种冷却方法视为本质上更简单的冷却方法之前，都应评估供应商支持、耗材、技术人员培训、保修程序、监控能力和长期服务访问。

冷却是一项设计要求，而不是附加项​

Blackwell Ultra GPU、双服务器 CPU、内存、网络、PCIe 交换和存储集中在 4U 外壳中，冷却与系统设计密不可分。 尽管将主要散热转移到液体冷却，华擎机架仍保留了大量的热插拔风扇容量。 所审查的机箱包括侧面的大型风扇托架以及系统下部中心的较小风扇模块。 该评论的后底盘检查突出了那些热插拔风扇和由此产生的气流路径。 这对潜在买家来说是一个重要的提醒：液体冷却并不意味着无风扇服务器。 气流对于内存、存储、电源、网络组件和其他板级硬件仍然是必需的。 冷却回路适用于最高功率的设备，但服务器的其余部分仍然需要弹性空气管理。

计算：Intel Xeon 6 提供主机平台​

华擎机架系统结合了八个 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPU 和两个 Intel Xeon 6 Granite Rapids 处理器。 在 HGX 服务器中，CPU 并不是主要的 AI 加速器，但其作用不应被低估。 它们协调操作系统服务、管理存储和网络 I/O、向 GPU 提供数据、托管控制平面软件，并提供使整个节点实用的 PCIe 和内存资源。 英特尔至强 6 P 核系列专为高性能服务器工作负载而设计，支持 AVX-512、高级矩阵扩展、DDR5、CXL 2.0 和大型 PCIe 5.0 I/O 配置等功能。 英特尔的 Xeon 6 产品简介列出了更广泛的系列中每个插槽最多 128 个 P 核、最多 12 个内存通道以及双插槽系统中最多 192 个 PCIe 5.0 通道。 单个华擎机架配置中的确切 CPU 选择、内存容量和 I/O 分配自然会因物料清单而异。 对于 Windows Server 管理员和虚拟化团队来说，主机端灵活性至关重要。 AI 基础设施越来越多地将 GPU 计算与数据预处理、存储服务、遥测代理、安全控制、编排组件和虚拟化工作负载混合在一起。 CPU 平台决定了这些相邻功能在不影响加速器利用率的情况下如何优雅地共存。 尽管如此，买家还是应该抵制仅根据 CPU 核心数量来判断 HGX B300 服务器的本能。 在此类机器中，主机处理器必须具有足够的功能和足够的连接；关键性能通常是 GPU 内存、NVLink 结构、网络拓扑、存储吞吐量、软件堆栈和工作负载行为之间的交互。

围绕平衡 I/O 构建的系统​

NVIDIA 的 HGX B300 参考设计强调平衡的 PCIe 拓扑，可跨 CPU 插槽和 PCIe 根端口分配连接。 它还为每个 HGX B300 基板定义了 8 个 PCIe Gen5 x16 链路和一个 Gen4 x2 链路。 NVIDIA 的 B300 系统要求明确指出，GPU 基板只是更广泛的 I/O 架构中的一个元素。 这就是为什么即使在 GPU 占主导地位的系统中，双至强设计仍然具有重要意义。 设计不当的主机平台可能会在存储摄取、管理网络、NIC 放置或设备位置方面造成瓶颈。 正确设计的双插槽实施为平台提供了保持 GPU 供电和连接的空间，而不会将整个系统减少到一系列妥协的权衡。

网络：前面板上的 6.4Tbps

华擎 Rack 4U16X-GNR2 最引人注目的操作细节可能是其八个前置 OSFP 笼，额定连接速度为 800Gbps。 该评测计算出前面板总带宽超过 6.4Tbps，无需单独的 PCIe 附加网卡。 ServeTheHome 的报告将这八个 OSFP 连接确定为机箱布局的一个定义特征。 这不是普通客户端流量的带宽。 这些端口对于系统作为集群节点的角色至关重要。 NVIDIA 的 HGX B300 设计采用八个 ConnectX-8 SuperNIC，在 GPU 和高速网络适配器之间提供一对一的关系，每个适配器高达 800Gbps。 NVIDIA 的 AI Factory 文档称，该配置旨在为东西向集群流量维持直接、高带宽的 GPU 到 NIC 连接。 实际上，这种结构将严格的多节点人工智能环境与一组强大但隔离的服务器分开。 在分布式训练过程中，不同节点上的 GPU 需要高效地交换梯度、参数和同步流量。 在大规模推理过程中，高速网络支持模型分片、请求分发、存储访问和服务扩展。 延迟、拥塞管理、布线、交换机设计和集体通信调整都会影响结果。

前置高速 I/O 具有真正的运营价值​

将最高速的网络连接放在前面可以使电缆布线在某些集群设计中更易于管理，特别是在首选冷通道服务访问和结构化机架前布线的情况下。 它还在 AI-fabric 连接和后向电力基础设施之间创建了视觉分离。 但前端接入 OSFP 连接并不自动适合每个设施。 网络架构、架空托盘路径、机架方向、收发器选择、光纤弯曲限制和交换机放置决定了部署是简化还是复杂化。 关键的优势并不是华擎 Rack 宣称一种布线方向普遍更好；而是而是服务器提供了一种经过深思熟虑的高密度网络布局，规划人员可以将其纳入更广泛的结构设计中。

存储和可维护性：专为物理数据中心而设计​

机箱正面，华擎机架提供 12 个 2.5 英寸 U.2 NVMe 托架。 根据审查，两个驱动器直接连接到 CPU，而十个驱动器通过 PCIe 交换机复合体连接。 ServeTheHome 的存储概览还显示了有线背板的布置。 该容量不会取代主要人工智能集群的专用并行存储系统。 尽管如此，它对于本地数据集暂存、检查点、缓存、启动映像、容器层、日志、临时训练工件和推理模型放置仍然很有价值。 在许多部署中，快速的本地 NVMe 对于避免对共享存储和网络结构造成不必要的压力至关重要。 前面板还包括四个 USB 3 Type-A 端口、VGA 输出和一个电源按钮。 这些并不是迷人的规格，但它们在启动、故障排除和现场服务过程中很重要。 为远程操作而构建的机器仍然必须忍受工程师站在带有急救车、可移动介质、诊断工具和有限时间的机架前的时刻。

灵活的管理-端口放置是一个安静的优势​

最实用的功能之一是管理和低速以太网连接的处理。 该系统在前面暴露了一个管理端口和两个基于 Intel i350 的 1GbE 端口，但内部以太网布线允许这些连接在后面重新定位。 审查指出，客户可以通过添加或删除相关的内部电缆来使用混合布置，例如，管理在前，1GbE 在后。 ServeTheHome 的机箱演练将该功能描述为一种支持多个数据中心布线约定且无需单独机箱 SKU 的方法。 这正是在总体规范中往往被忽视但基础设施团队所赞赏的设计决策。 管理网络通常遵循与数据结构不同的物理路径、安全边界或操作所有权模型。 为客户提供一种将这些端口放置在其所属位置的方法，可以减少尴尬的电缆布线并避免不必要的采购碎片化。

功率、冗余和密度成本​

根据审查，该平台的后部装有 10 个 3kW 80 Plus Titanium 电源模块以实现冗余；它的文字将它们标记为“CPU”，但随附的上下文和图像描述清楚地表明这些是电源。 因此，最初的演练应被理解为记录冗余的 3kW Titanium 级 PSU，而不是不寻常的十处理器配置。 十个大容量电源的存在就说明了真实的情况。 该平台专为满足巨大的电力需求、容错能力以及在个别 PSU 故障时维持服务的能力而设计。 这也表明购买服务器只是财务承诺的开始。 成功的部署需要：

  • 适当的机架配电，可能包括高压三相馈电。
  • 电源容量规划涵盖最坏情况下的节点行为，而不仅仅是平均利用率。
  • 冷却能力符合液体回路和残余气流的要求。
  • 能够处理 800Gbps 级连接和 AI 通信模式的交换结构。
  • 存储基础设施的大小适合模型数据、检查点、数据集和保留策略。
  • 监控和编排工具可以观察 GPU、热量、结构运行状况、电源、固件和工作负载行为。

电源是冗余的，但冗余并不能消除依赖性。 服务器的有效性与其周围的上游电源和冷却系统密不可分。

风险和部署注意事项​

华擎 Rack 4U16X-GNR2 的优势也决定了其风险。 这是一个功能异常强大的平台，但它不能容忍不完整的规划。

设施准备就绪是第一位​

第一个风险是将液体冷却视为孤立的硬件功能。 直接液冷服务器属于能够正确供应、监控和维修冷却回路的设施。 在安装机架之前，应规划流量、冷却剂温度、水质、连接器程序、泄漏响应、维护窗口和备件策略。 ZutaCore 变体可能会吸引在芯片级寻求介电、无水方法的组织，但它仍然是专门的冷却基础设施。 它改变了实施方式，而不是消除了对运营专业知识的需求。

网络投资可以与服务器投资相媲美​

八个 800Gbps OSFP 连接提供了非凡的潜力，但它们也提出了同样非凡的基础设施要求。 服务器需要兼容的收发器或电缆、高密度交换、足够的上行链路、拥塞管理专业知识以及配置为有效使用结构的 AI 软件堆栈。 连接到规模过小或调整不当的网络的 B300 节点将无法提供其架构旨在实现的分布式工作负载行为。 节点的速度增加了结构错误的惩罚。

软件堆栈仍然是产品的核心部分​

NVIDIA 的 HGX 平台文档不仅强调 GPU 硬件，还强调 NVLink、网络、优化的 AI 软件、结构管理和虚拟化支持。 NVIDIA 的 HGX 平台文档包括 Fabric Manager、NVSwitch 桥接补丁和共享 NVSwitch GPU 直通虚拟化的专用材料。 这有力地表明，操作 HGX 平台是一项系统工程任务，而不仅仅是驱动程序安装工作。 Windows Server 环境可以参与企业 AI 工作流程，特别是在管理、数据准备、Active Directory 集成、文件服务、开发人员工具和虚拟化基础设施方面。 然而，在选择 HGX 平台之前，组织应验证其 AI 应用程序所需的确切操作系统、驱动程序、容器、框架和编排组合。 硬件足够强大，软件不兼容、不受支持的配置或不成熟的操作实践都可能成为限制因素。

底线​

华擎机架 4U16X-GNR2 是一个令人印象深刻的例子，展示了当密度被视为工程目标而不是营销统计数据时，现代 NVIDIA HGX B300 服务器的外观。 其八个 Blackwell Ultra GPU、NVLink/NVSwitch 扩展结构、双 Intel Xeon 6 主机处理器、12 个 U.2 NVMe 托架、前端接入 800Gbps OSFP 网络、可配置管理端口布局、热插拔风扇和冗余大容量电源设计构成了一个适用于严肃 AI 基础设施的连贯平台。 最初的华擎机架系统审查使这种集成在机箱级别可见。 它最重要的成就可能是拒绝将 GPU 视为独立组件。 4U16X-GNR2 认识到 AI 性能最终由整个节点决定：GPU 内存容量、高速互连、CPU 和 PCIe 拓扑、NVMe 布局、网络带宽、热设计、电源冗余以及管理员部署和修复的难易程度。 对于具备必要的电源、冷却、结构和软件成熟度的企业、云提供商、研究机构和 AI 服务运营商来说，这正是可以锚定高性能 AI 集群的密集 8 GPU 服务器。 对于其他人来说，这是一个有说服力的演示，表明 Blackwell Ultra 性能之路贯穿数据中心架构，而不仅仅是通过购买更多 GPU。
